utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we start I think I have to remind you of something. We understand that you are eager to give your testimony in this courtroom to help the Judges to understand what was happening in July 1995 in Srebrenica. But the proceeding in this courtroom is quite different from where you come from. Generally speaking, the witness should be led by the party who asks questions. In most of all occasions, all those answers -- all those questions could be answered simply by saying yes or no. If the counsel needs more information on certain subjects, he could ask the follow-up questions. So I hope your answer to each question could be as concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We left off yesterday when you spoke to us about your meeting with Colonel Beara. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before we get into that event and what happened afterwards, I just want to get some things out of the way. You were questioned by the Prosecution, were you not?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you were questioned, I believe the date was 10 December 2003.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not getting a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were questioned by the Prosecution, were you questioned as a witness or as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they came, they told me I would be interviewed as a suspect, and then I was interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may have a moment. I'm having some problems. I can hear the translations through somebody else's, but I'm having a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you understand that as you sit here today and as you're testifying, you still have the status of suspect. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it that's making you a little nervous?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That was leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, in this occasion, I don't think -- well, it is a leading question but in this occasion I don't think it matters very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you were questioned in Banja Luka as a suspect almost four years after the Prosecution indicted Mr. Blagojevic, some two years after he was arrested, were you informed as to the reasons why you were deemed a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me, I would like to make a correction. This was not in Banja Luka but in Bratunac, in my office, where I was interviewed. I was never told why I was considered a suspect. That is, at the beginning I wasn't told. Later on, they mentioned Resid Sinanovic as the person who is implied as a participant in the events in which I allegedly participated as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We're going to go step by step. And in fact, you had an opportunity to read the indictment by the Prosecution -- or one of them at least, one -- not the latest one that they're proposing, but the one before, 17 June 2003. Correct? You've looked at that indictment?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, on paragraph 47.5 is where it's referenced -- and I'll just read it for the record to make sure that we are on the same point. It says: "At some time from 12 July through 1 November 1995, six Bosnian Muslim men from Srebrenica were captured by MUP forces, turned over to and interrogated by security personnel from the Bratunac Brigade under the command and control of Vidoje Blagojevic and under the directions of Momir Nikolic and thereafter summarily executed by unknown persons." And then it says: "One of these persons, Resid Sinanovic, was captured by MUP soldiers from the Republika Srpska RS, turned over personally to Momir Nikolic before being executed." Do you recall reading that portion of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But it's this -- is it not -- is it Resid Sinanovic or the issue of the whereabouts of Resid Sinanovic that has -- that you've been told is the reasons for you being a suspect?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you question Resid Sinanovic in Bratunac shortly after the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you summarily execute him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you execute anyone, as being suggested by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before we go into what happened to him --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This -- it appears to be an intent to inflame the witness. First of all in suggesting to him that he's nervous because of what an investigator has a duty to tell him, and now he's saying the Prosecution suggested he executed someone. There's no suggestion in that. It's part of the interrogation process of people that were executed. This is well-known. And to say that to this man is really unconscionable. For him to go back and suggest that we say he's an executioner; that's just not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think we remind you many times, do not mention the Prosecution, or mention the Prosecution as little as possible. In your question it is not necessary to add that phrase "as being suggested by the Prosecution." The question is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'll go about it in another way, Your Honour, because I do believe that there is some worries from this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you read -- when you were informed about the summary execution of Resid Sinanovic, what came to your mind?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think anything, because earlier I saw a paragraph from the indictment in which it does say that he was summarily executed, but this wasn't the case. I know that this wasn't the case. I did see him, and if it says in the indictment that he died and before that he had seen me, that means that I was somehow involved, but I was not involved in an ugly way. And I was really concerned because in the indictment there are some facts which may be linked to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, do you know what happened to Resid Sinanovic after you -- after he left you? Just briefly tell us, do you know what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left to the collection centre, which was in the school, like everybody else. And now I know that on the 14th of December, 1995, he was sent for treatment in Banja Koviljaca in Serbia -- that is, in Yugoslavia, a day after I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, is that December or could it be another month?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in July. 14 July. I may have misspoken, and I would like to correct myself. The 14th of July I saw the document according to which he was in that town on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you what has been marked as -- for identification purposes as D169. Please look at these documents. Just look at them first, and we're going to go step by step. Do you recognise these documents?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what are these documents?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a letter sent by Milenko Marin from Loznica. He was the director of the health centre, and it was sent to a lawyer Londrovic from Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First, I'm going to ask you to slow down. Slow down, because everything is being translated, okay? Who was it sent to? Could you please repeat the name again.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's all right. We're all nervous here.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was sent to Veselin Londrovic, attorney-at-law, by Dr. Milenko Marin, the director of the medical centre in Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. How did you get a hold of this document -- let me back up. Have you seen this document before? Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How did you -- how did it come to your possession? How is it that you saw it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally asked Mr. Veselin Londrovic, attorney-at-law from Bijeljina, to tell me whether he had such a document in his possession. This is the person who represented Mr. Momir Nikolic, this attorney-at-law. Should I tell you the reason why I wanted to see this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the reason, step by step. What was the reason for asking for the document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked for this document for the following reason: I was very worried after the visit of the representatives of The Hague Tribunal and the conversation that I had with them in December 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why were you concerned? What was the nature of your concern?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was concerned because the alleged death or disappearance of Resid Sinanovic had nothing whatsoever to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us what the next document is, the one that you received and Mr. Londrovic received.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photocopy of the title page of the logbook from the year 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And is there any particular section on this page, the photocopied page - and that would be on page 3 of the English version - is there any portion of it that is relevant to what we are discussing right now?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I understand -- I can see that on the left-hand side of the page we have some numbers. Could you please read out the number that is relevant.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you will allow me, the date is more relevant than the number itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But if you will allow me, let me walk you through. First, which part --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No worries. Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I apologise. This number is 2028.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go through -- if we go across the page, what does it say there in Srpski?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbian it says: "Resid Sinanovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And further down, if we go over, does it have a date of birth that you can read?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see 19, but the last two digits are illegible. I can't read the last two digits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if you go further down, where it says street number, residence, place of municipality, what does it say there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Srebrenica," and underneath it says "Bratunac," but the word "Bratunac" is crossed out, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you ever -- what is this document -- and what is the date for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, is the second page relevant?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Incidentally, before we get to the second page, under date, the second column -- if you go back to the first page, sir. Mr. Celanovic, if I could direct your attention to the first page, where it says "date." Okay. I want you to look at the column 2026. Do you see a date there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the date is 15 July. Now I can see it. Yes, 15 July. I apologise. I only looked at the top of the page before, just the first entry on the top of that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, sir, if we go further down, to 2028, it would appear that that would be the date, 15 July 1995. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that name under that number is that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we go to the second page, is there anything significant that we need to be aware of?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the third column from the bottom towards the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. What about it? What does it say there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "Dr. Bozica" in the top left corner. In the right upper corner of that column, it says the treatment of wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what treatment did he receive? What treatment does it appear that this gentleman by the name of Resid received?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what wound he had or if he had any at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you allow me to read this to the end?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Underneath, it says that he was referred to the surgical department. And underneath again, it says admitted and then returned to the surgical department again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, these documents, after you received them from Mr. Londrovic, did you do anything with them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried to deliver this document to the investigator of The Hague Tribunal who had interviewed me. His name is Alistair Graham. This is what I read on the card that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we've come across that name before. Well, did you -- did he accept the documents?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Alistair did not refuse to accept the documents; however -- may I continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to him on the phone, and I informed him that I had a written document, and I meant this document that I have before me as we speak, and that this document confirmed that my statement given to him, to Mr. Alistair Graham, was truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me that I could fax this document to him, but that I should wait a little for him to check whether the Prosecution had that document already. Maybe he had it already he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did he get back to you? Did Mr. Graham return -- get back to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't get back to me; I called him two, maybe three times. I wanted to be sure that they would receive my fax, that -- when I sent it. I spoke to Mr. Alistair again and he told me that due to the holiday period in January -- and during that holiday period he would again come to Bratunac and that if I had that document -- or if he had that document, that he would bring it with him, because he would have had the time to check whether he had it and to bring it with him. If he didn't have that document, on the other hand, then he would take it from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did he ever come to pick up the document or to show you a copy of the document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ever manage to fax it or deliver it to Alistair Graham, who was an investigator for the Office of the Prosecution working directly on this case?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in April. I believe it was the end of April when I was submitted a transcript of my interview with Alistair, as well as a CD, and when I was told that I had been proposed to be the Defence counsel and that they could not contact me as such any longer -- any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would have been April 2004?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, this year. Yes, yes. I apologise because of my imprecision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, since we're with -- we're talking about Resid Sinanovic. I want to stay with him and I want to discuss what happened. First of all, did you know Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, who is -- how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were good colleagues, the two of us. We were good friends. We were both fishermen, anglers, we were comrades. This is as much as I can put into this description. Need I say more?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was he an educated man, Mr. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was a jurist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what -- prior to the war, where did Mr. Sinanovic live?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He lived in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what position -- what kind of work did Mr. Sinanovic do?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while he performed the duty of head of the police station, of the SUP. And the last post which he held over the last year or two years, I'm not quite sure, was this post that he had with the decorative ceramic tiles factory in Bratunac as a secretary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was the same factory where in 1995 the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were located. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the same factory, but when I used to visit him prior to the war, he was sitting in the building where the military police was, or rather, his office was there, and that also belonged to the same. It was a detached building of the same factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just for a point of clarification, earlier you said that he was with the Bratunac Brigade -- I mean, with the -- he was with the police department, and it says here "SUP." He was head of the police station of the SUP. Would that be MUP, M-U-P?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when the war broke out, do you know what happened to Mr. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he fled Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know where he went?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he went. Probably to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you talked a little bit yesterday about your position in interviewing prisoners of war that were brought to you. Were you at any point in time made aware of Mr. Sinanovic being a potential or an alleged war criminal?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what the circumstances were. What had you learned?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I probably already mentioned that I participated in the collection of information about the war crimes committed by Muslims against the Serbs - I mean in Srebrenica and Bratunac - and that in the process I had occasion to hear, in taking statements from the Serbian civilians who had survived massacres in the Serbian villages. Namely, some of them mentioned Resid Sinanovic as a person who had participated in the attack on the village of Bjelovac. However, these statements associated with him were not at all logical and that is why I did not indeed accept them as serious statements. Nevertheless, his name came to feature on record as a person suspected of war crimes in the book which I referred to yesterday written by the author Ivanisevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you place his name or forward his name to be placed in that book? Because if I believe your previous testimony, you were forwarding information to a commission regarding alleged war criminals.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. There was no grounds for that whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when -- in 1995 in July, after the fall of Srebrenica, did you get an opportunity to see Mr. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, if you recall, the date.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 13th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where you saw him.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him at my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us how it is that Mr. Sinanovic came to your office or appeared at your office.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was brought there by Mr. Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall -- I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps the volume is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And if you have any problems with hearing, let us know. Okay. Now, when Mr. Nikolic brought him over there, did Mr. Nikolic say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No translation. I'm getting no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot reply, not having heard your question translated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Don't panic. Don't panic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no panic, in fact. I apologise, but that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's all right. That's all right. When Momir Nikolic brought Mr. Sinanovic over, did he say anything to you? Mr. Nikolic, that is.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what he told you.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me there -- actually, he got a hold of me outside, in the courtyard. He told me: Here, look, I've brought your colleague Resid Sinanovic. Come with me to the office. Take a look at these statements that you have, because he has been suspected of war crimes, and look in your statements whether you have anything serious which would attest to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us about what time of day it would have been on the 13th of July, 1995, that Momir Nikolic brought Mr. Sinanovic over to your office.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the morning hours, sometime around 10.00 or 11.00. I cannot say with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And after Mr. Nikolic told you that he had brought your colleague, Mr. Sinanovic, what did you and perhaps even Mr. Nikolic do?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we entered the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you entered the office, could you please explain to us, in what condition did you find Mr. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My colleague Mr. Resid Sinanovic looked tired, but he looked physically sound, unhurt. He was sitting there on a chair. As I came in, we greeted each other normal fashion, like normal people. We struck -- we started talking to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the meanwhile, Momir Nikolic said goodbye to Resid and he went out. He said: I'm going out to the terrain, and that's what he said; goodbye.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, was Mr. Sinanovic restrained in any way? Did he have any handcuffs on him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us, after Momir Nikolic left your office to go to the terrain, as he had said, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went on talking with Mr. Sinanovic. It was only normal for us to talk to each other. We hadn't seen each other for four years, so we sat there, and I offered him some coffee, which he accepted, and I also offered him some snacks and he had a bit to eat. I also offered what cigarettes I had and also a glass of brandy. So whatever I had, I offered to him. And we talked about everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long -- I didn't mean to interrupt you there. How long did you talk with Mr. Sinanovic, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, initially for about 45 minutes or half an hour. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you had been given some instructions from Mr. Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But I have -- okay. Well, if I could refer back to your earlier statement or your earlier comments, Mr. Nikolic had asked you, had he not, to look to some -- to see whether there was any information regarding the allegations against Mr. Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise, I did not get your last question correctly, and if that is it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. No need to apologise. Now, did you have a conversation with Mr. Sinanovic regarding any activities he might have been involved in or anyone else might have been involved in concerning war crimes?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told him this: I told him that I already had a position of my own on the question, namely -- well, I cannot exactly say what I said on that occasion because I had to be courteous in this court. I said there was no reason for him to have been labelled in this way at all, especially given the fact that, in addition to him, his wife had also been labelled as such and that I thought -- it was my position that he had nothing whatsoever to do with it and that he should not be worried at all. And then we didn't talk about it anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you collect any other information from him with respect to the Muslim fighters that were in Srebrenica but had --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you by any chance memorialise, take notes, regarding your conversation with Mr. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you what has been marked as P476 and has come into evidence in fact. A is the English version, B is the handwritten version. Take your time. Please look at the document first. When you're through looking at it, let me know and I'll ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, do you recognise the handwriting on this document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And do you recognise the subject matter that is in this document that bears your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a record of the statement of Resid Sinanovic, but rather, his account of things than a formal statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And do these notes reflect the nature of your conversation with respect to the events surrounding -- the Muslim population that had left Srebrenica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we look at this document, it would appear that there is information on this document that might be relevant to your commander or to the security organ or intelligence organ. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My first question is: Did you pass this document on to anyone, or this information on to anyone up the chain of command so at least they would be aware of what Mr. Sinanovic had told you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Sorry. I thought you had completed your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you share this information with Momir Nikolic, the individual who had brought Resid Sinanovic to your office?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you share this information with Colonel Beara in any way?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you share this information with your commander, Colonel Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, considering that, as we've discussed yesterday, at one point during this war you had activities related to counter-intelligence activities, or the gathering of counter-intelligence information, could you please tell us why you did not share this information with anyone.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The data contained in this note actually reflects a spontaneous conversation between Resid Sinanovic and myself. And basically I told him what my role on that day was, to try and record the people, or rather, to check whether the people being brought in were on the list of suspects of war crimes against the civilian population. He was aware of this role of my mine, and I asked him and told him that it would be very useful if he knew anything - after all, he knew what I was doing - to tell me where -- if he knew where Naser's commanders were with the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In particular, where the commanders were, because all of them had been, in a way, on record as suspects for war crimes committed against civilians in attacking Serbian villages and torching Serbian villages when a lot of people died.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But specifically I want to focus your attention to the language in your notes where it states that: "This morning, about a thousand to 1.500 armed men remained. About 6 to 7.000 remained in the spot where the shells landed." And it goes on. This information would appear to be somewhat significant, in light of the fact that we're talking about armed Muslim men whom you knew had committed, or were accused of having committed atrocities against the Serbs. Did you not think it was necessary for you to bring this to anyone's attention so they could act upon it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because according to the order from Mr. Beara, I was not supposed to focus on that particular part. This is just an account by Resid Sinanovic without him having been asked any specific questions. So I just put it down so it would be obvious that I had indeed conducted this conversation with him. And secondly, in the classical and conventional sense, one could not use this particular bit of information at all because we had a moving army and moving people, movement of the people and of troops. So it was not a question of the day; it was a question of a situation changing from hour to hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And actually, no one wanted me to -- required me to pass on such information to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Celanovic, before we talk about what happened during your visit with Mr. Sinanovic, I want to take the opportunity to inform you that during this trial a Prosecution witness, former employee of theirs, Richard Butler, indicated - and I'm reading from page 4.486, lines 10 through 12 - that: "These interrogation notes were found in the security office of the Bratunac or of the former Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade during the OTP search." That's a quote/unquote from the record on 13 November 2003. You've just told us that you didn't pass this information on to Momir Nikolic, whom we all know was the head of security and intelligence of the Bratunac Brigade. Would you please explain to us how it is that these notes then landed in his office.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a fact that I never handed over these notes to him. After I compiled them, I put them somewhere in my office, in one of the drawers. They were insignificant; I didn't even give it a second thought. How they came to end up in Momir Nikolic's office, I have no idea. I have no explanation. Maybe after I started working in the civilian sector -- I find it inexplicable, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me help you out here, or perhaps you can help us out. We know, having heard the testimony of one Ruez, who was the chief investigator at the time, that some years after commencing the investigation in this case at about 1998, he received -- he got the documents from what he believed to have been the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade. Could you please tell us, in 1998, where was the Bratunac Brigade located? Where were their offices located at that point in time, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know that the headquarters of the Bratunac Brigade at the time -- was relocated at the time to the former building of the military police, which I already referred to as the auxiliary building in front of the gate to the ceramic tiles factory called Kaolin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And that would have been --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it was in another place. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would have been the same building where your offices were located back in 1995. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps that might assist us in figuring out why they ended up there. Now, getting back to Resid Sinanovic, while he was in your office did anyone else visit him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us who.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A friend of his from Bratunac, Srbislav Davidovic, aka Buco.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was Mr. Davidovic's position at that point in time, in the community of Bratunac, that is, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was a civilian working with the municipal authorities. And also, he had this duty which he had performed for many years, that is, the peoples' university director. I'm not sure what he was at that particular point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us, if you can, how is it that Mr. Davidovic knew that Mr. Sinanovic was in your office at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how he came by that information. He only told me that he had heard that Momir had brought Resid in, and he asked whether he could see him. So he heard from somebody; I don't know who from. Obviously I allowed him to come into my office, because the three of us were colleagues and even friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us what, if anything, happened or what, if anything, was discussed when Mr. Davidovic was there visiting you and Mr. Sinanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was an informal conversation about life and things of that sort. We didn't talk about the army or anything of that sort. I left the office for a while. The two of them were better friends than Resid and I, so I thought it would be a courteous thing for me to step out of the office and leave the two of them alone. I was standing in front of the building for about an hour. I was in the courtyard of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then I returned to my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know about how long Mr. Davidovic visited?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. After Mr. Davidovic left, what did you -- what happened or what did you do with Mr. Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked some more, and then he was taken away to the school, which was a collection centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. First of all, how long was Mr. Sinanovic there before he was, as you put it, taken away to the school which was the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An hour or two hours from the moment when he first came to the moment when he was taken to the collection centre. It could have been less or maybe more. I don't know for a fact. I didn't pay too much attention to the time that he spent in my office. I didn't look at the watch. And even if I had, I would have forgotten by now. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please tell us, who came by to take him away? Who were these individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of a unit which was not from Bratunac. I didn't know them. They were the same soldiers who, immediately after Nikolic had brought Resid in, also brought some five or six other people, whose particulars I took while I was standing outside while Srbislav and Resid were talking in my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know whether they were part of the military or whether they were part of MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were part of the military. They had a coat of arms of Republika Srpska. I didn't know -- I didn't see which unit they belonged to. I didn't come any closer. They were rather arrogant. I believe that they belonged to a special military police unit, because they were in charge of taking this group of people to the school to hand them over to the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did they have any -- other than the coat of arms that you were able to note, did they have any other insignia or any other -- any other insignia, let's stay with that, that would indicate whether they were soldiers or part of the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see anything. They may have had something, but I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall whether their uniforms had any distinct colours or anything that would set them out, set them apart?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No special colours. They had military overalls, good-quality military overalls, of the sort that our troops in Bratunac didn't have. Some did, but not all of them. They had different sorts of uniforms. And judging by their behaviour and their appearance, they were members of some important unit; they were not from the Bratunac Brigade. I didn't dare ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me just walk you through. All right. First of all, did they inform you who their commander was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they inform you who had instructed them to come to the Bratunac Brigade to either bring prisoners to you or to take prisoners away from you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said you didn't ask them. Is there a particular reason why you didn't ask them, you know: Who are you? What are you doing? On whose instructions you are here?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a reason. They appeared and asked for somebody to point them in the direction of the school, because they were there to take these people to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When they came to take Resid Sinanovic away - someone who you knew as a colleague and as a friend, who you had concluded, even before meeting him, that he was not a war criminal - why did you not refuse to give Mr. Sinanovic to these individuals to take him away to the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I believed that they were following a procedure and that Resid was not threatened in any way. By being taken to the collection centre, he would stay alive, that there was no threat for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that point in time, sir, did you know what was going to happen to the individuals -- or what did you think would happen to the individuals, I should say, that were taken to the collection centre?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't think anything would happen to him. I simply thought that once he was in the collection centre, that they would all be transported to Kladanj, Tuzla, Zvornik, or the nearest part of the territory under the control of the Muslim armed forces. I believed that these people would just be evacuated, as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was the basis of this belief?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no reason for me to believe anything else or think anything else. It would not be logical for me to believe or think anything else. How could I ever think that somebody had the intention to hurt, harm, or kill so many people? And my belief was spontaneously corroborated by my conversation with Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, we're going to get to that. We're going to get to Colonel Beara. Now, were you in Potocari on that day or the day before?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In front of Potocari, or before Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you go to Potocari where the mass of people were located that had come from Srebrenica and were there with the Dutch?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From where you had gone to -- first of all, how far towards Potocari you had gone? You know that there's a yellow bridge as you leave Bratunac and before you get to Potocari; had you passed the yellow bridge, checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far past the checkpoint had you gone toward Potocari?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drove as far as the building of Elektrodistribucija, which is at the entrance to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall what day that was that you drove to this location?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Maybe on the same day when Resid was in my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you recall what time of day it was when you drove to that location?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Midday. After 1.00 in the afternoon maybe, but I can't be sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us, what were the reasons for you going to that location?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there by accident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, one doesn't get to one location by accident. You had to --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Can I explain then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Initially I wanted to go to Vihor, to my company. I wanted to take some stationery, some paper and carbon paper. I was short on supplies in my office. I passed by the medical centre and I saw Dr. Vesna Ivanovic and a nurse who asked me to give them a lift. We talked, and I believe that they were a team on duty to -- who were being sent to the place where there was a lot of people gathering. I took them to the building of Elektrodistribucija and some 100 or 150 metres in front of me I saw a convoy of members of the United Nations across the road, and behind them I saw a crowd of people. I left the two of them there because I had some chores to do. I went to my office to fetch the stationery, and then I returned. That's why I say I found myself there by accident, because I didn't have any intention of going there in the first place. I didn't have any reason to find myself there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just a couple of questions before we -- short ones, hopefully. Did you get out of your car at that point to walk around?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this might be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break and we'll resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we hear the witness, are there any matters? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think we can save some time by me just clarifying an issue, and I've spoken to Mr. Karnavas about this briefly. At the break I talked to Mr. Graham to refresh my recollection on the subject matter of these medical records of -- possible medical records of Resid Sinanovic. And Mr. Graham did acknowledge that he did have communications with this witness regarding those documents, and that was at a time prior to Momir Nikolic's plea. And the witness did tell us that he had received these documents from Mr. Nikolic's lawyer. And so what Mr. Graham had said is that, well, we are not sure we can get this material at this time, given that it may be confidential material. And so that's why there was a delay. In April, after I believe the matter with Mr. Nikolic was resolved, Bruce Bursik was in Bratunac and did meet with the witness and picked up these -- copies of these materials. And shortly thereafter, in May, those materials were provided to the Defence. So Mr. Shin won't be asking too many questions, hopefully, on that topic as I think that sort of should have clarified it. And I didn't think it was a big enough issue to worry about rebuttal witnesses and that sort of thing. And I think Mr. Karnavas agrees with me that this should at least clear it up for now, unless anyone has any more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have nothing to add. I think it's a perfectly acceptable explanation. Circumstantial evidence, we can see how it can sometimes lead us to the wrong conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I have no comments on that. Well, could we have the witness, please. Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, now I believe you indicated that at some point there were several other Muslim males that came or were brought to you for you to question. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that there were some other men, Muslim men, who were not brought to me for interrogation. They were brought because the soldiers who escorted them didn't know where the school was. And I explained to those soldiers what my role was on that day, and they understood that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you question any of those individuals, those Muslim men that were with those soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you make notes of that questioning?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, could you please -- we began -- first of all, let me ask you: Why did you question those individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not a classical interrogation. My obligation was to find out who these people were, where they were headed, and how they had reached Bratunac. Another thing that I was supposed to ask them was whether they were aware of the whereabouts of Naser's commanders, for the reasons that I have already explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on whose orders or instructions were you questioning these individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Ljubisa Beara's orders and instructions, who was a high-ranking security officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I don't know if I asked you this question yesterday, and if I have I apologise, but when Mr. Beara gave you this order, did you inform Colonel Blagojevic that you were conducting this questioning?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm told that perhaps the translation was not accurate, so let me ask the question again. When Colonel Beara gave -- issued this order to you, did you inform your commander, Colonel Blagojevic, that you had been instructed by Colonel Beara to carry out this activity?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know where Commander Blagojevic was, and I was never asked to inform Commander Blagojevic about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me show you some documents, a list of documents. And for the sake of time I'm going to hand you what has been marked for identification as P477, P478, and P479. I believe these documents have been introduced into evidence already. If you could look at -- if you could look at those documents and first of all please tell us if you recognise the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And whose handwriting is it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall when you made these notations?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When was it that you made these notations?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what were these notations in relation to? Why were they made?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They referred to my identification of the persons who had been brought, and the purpose was to see whether any of them was on record as a suspect of war crimes against the civilian Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you also question these individuals with respect to others who might be on any lists?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First, I identified these persons, and you can find their names here. None of these individuals had been recorded on any lists of suspect, save for Resid Sinanovic. In order to curtail the whole procedure, I focused on finding out from them where Naser's commanders were. Those are a few people whose names are mentioned here. Not all of them, but some of them. And that's the kind of answers they gave me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what happened to these notes once you completed them? What did you do with them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left them in my office, either on one of the shelves or in my desk, because nothing significant had happened. None of these persons were identified as suspects. To my mind, their record was clean, and then they were taken to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me stop you there. How long did you question these individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple minutes, three minutes, five minutes, depending on how much they had to tell me. And then I made some very informal notes on the conversations that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did this questioning take place?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside. In front of the building in which my office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if you had --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if you had an office that was only a few metres away, why didn't you question them in your office?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During that time, Resid Sinanovic and Srbislav Davidovic were in my office for an hour; they were talking there. And even if they hadn't been there, I would have still talked to these people outside, because it was very, very hot. And my conversation with these people was informal, in the shade. There was no need for me to take them to my office and waste time in this very, very hot room.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the individuals that brought -- the soldiers that brought these Muslim men to you, where were they when you were conducting this questioning?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How were these Muslim men brought to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. They were brought in front of the military police building, and these soldiers asked for directions to the elementary school in which would be accommodated, i.e., receive these Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me get back to my question: How were they brought there by these soldiers? Were they on foot? Were they in a particular vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand the question. They were in a vehicle, and this vehicle is called, in soldiers' lingo, the 110 vehicle. It is a small truck, in fact, intended for personnel, i.e., troops, transportation, because it has seats, and of course cargo can also be transported. I cannot tell you the exact make and manufacture of the car, and this was a designation that was used by us all, 110.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would that be a 110 TAM, T-A-M? Is that what we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I wasn't sure of the make. It is probably a T-A-M 110, because we had many vehicles manufactured for the army by TAM.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know from which unit this vehicle was from?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I believe in one of your previous answers you talked about -- you indicated that none of the individuals that you spoke with were on any lists, correct, at least any lists that you were aware of. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except for Resid Sinanovic, who I believe was recorded in the book, but these other persons weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you what has come into evidence as P442. 442/B is the Srpski version; A is the English version. Could you just look at that list first of all.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I looked at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, according to -- again, the former employee of the Office of the Prosecution, Richard Butler, on page 4.440 he indicated that he believed that: "In January or February 1998, these documents were found at the headquarters of the former Bratunac Brigade, specifically in the office of the security officer of the Bratunac Brigade." That would be found on lines 19 through 22. So could you please explain to us, first of all, whether you had seen this list.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not my list, nor have I seen it -- had I ever seen it before, except for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And of course, going back to your earlier answer, in 1998 the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were located in the facilities where your office was located in 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, back in 1995, where was Mr. Momir Nikolic's office located, if you know, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know where it was. It was in the headquarters building of the brigade, headquarters brigade, which is the factory building within the compound of the clay or ceramic factory, which is to say outside the building where my office was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, first of all, in looking at this document, the one that you have, do you -- can you recognise the typing machine which might have generated this particular document? Would this be one that was in your possession, in your office, at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This text was typewritten by an electric machine whereas the typewriter which I used throughout that period was a mechanical one and it didn't have this particular shape of letters. I am well-versed in machines, and this was typewritten on an electrical machine - I mean typewriter - that I never had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, to the best of your knowledge, you never saw this, you did not have this list back in July 1995. Is that correct? Is that what you're stating?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I never saw this list, and as I stated I used this book, Chronicle of Our Graveyards, which has systematised material with the names of the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you were questioned by the Office of the Prosecution back on 10 December 2003, do you recall whether this list was shown to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was not shown to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, have you had a chance before coming here today, before testifying under oath, to look at this list?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the list that you showed me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, is this the same list? That's what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Can it be put more precisely, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Before coming here today to testify, okay -- and we know the Prosecutor never showed you the document, but before coming to testify here, did you have a chance to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before taking the stand today, I saw this document during the proofing, the preparations for testifying before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was a couple of days ago?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before -- before I entered this courtroom for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in looking at this list, do you recognise the names on the list, or at least some of the names on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do recognise some of the names, and I have recognised some of them. And given the nature of this list, some of these names should certainly not be on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you give us a representative example.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are a number of them, but I will give you an example. Just a minute, please. Bear with me until I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perhaps it might save some time if I were to present you with my copy. And I will ask some foundational questions first.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me show you --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- another copy of P442/B. On that particular copy, sir, you see some highlighted -- a blue highlight on the page, do you not? Some of the names have been highlighted. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us, who placed those highlights there?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I highlighted those names. I highlighted them when I was going through the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And just -- we don't have to go through all of them, but if you could read out the number of some of those highlights and please tell us or give us your opinion with respect to some of the names that occur on this list --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- that you believe have no reason to be on this list.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what is wrong with number 15?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 16 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Cekaj. Hold on for one second. As we go through each name, I would like you to give a short explanation as to why you believe this individual should not be on the list. Okay. So number 15. Okay, who is this person and why is it your belief --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I think that will be fine, Mr. Usher, so you don't have to trouble yourself.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So number 15, Dzevad, father Hamed, Gusic, born in 1960 in Bratunac. I know him personally. He was or is still a deputy of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, and he performed the -- the same duty as I did in Bratunac is what he did in the Srebrenica armed forces, but there was never any report of any untoward behaviour on the part of this person and he should not be on this list definitely. I should like to know that on the list we have organisers of war crimes. So prior to the war, he never participated in any such crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to need you to speak a little slower. Okay. All right. So on this list, if I understand you correctly, you do recognise names which you believe were accused or were alleged to have committed war crimes.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what other names on this -- on the first page that you see should not be on this list?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 16, Izet, father Sulejman, Gusic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Can you please tell us why you think this individual shouldn't be on the list.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because no one ever heard of him having done anything ugly, and specifically nothing of the kind that these people on the list are alleged to have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Anybody else?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are many of them, many more of them, if you will allow me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Just pick a sample. We don't have to go through the entire list.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a sample, 71 and 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurija, father Hamdija, Dzanic; and Salcin, father Hamdija, Dzanic. These are people who fled from Bratunac sometime in March 1992. They were not in the area of Bratunac and Srebrenica during the war in the first place. They had no opportunity to do what they are alleged to have done. And these are decent people and should certainly not be on this list which was made arbitrarily by someone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are more, if you will allow me. I don't know how much time we have. Let me just tell you the numbers. It is, for instance, 35, Enver Kubat, a physician, a doctor, who might have been in Srebrenica possibly performing his duties as a doctor. And another example -- no, there are many examples, and I would be happy as to read all of them so you would know that these were decent people. And out of respect of those people I would like to read out all of their names. They were Muslims, but of course they were decent people in my mind. May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, for the sake of time, let me ask a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are there any women on this list?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in your opinion, were these women alleged to have been war criminals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What are the others?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never heard of these others. This one I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's number 23.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 323, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know who might have compiled this list?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no idea who could have compiled this list, but that someone was not very critical in compiling this list, but perhaps was tendentious, because this list should certainly not include some of these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In light of your position of having to question the occasional prisoner of war, were you ever provided a list by Momir Nikolic, the commander for intelligence and security for the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember having ever been provided any list by him. It was rather that he received lists from me, partial ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I think that's about it for this particular list.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, let's go back to July 13th. You indicated you had the occasion to question certain individuals that were brought over by some soldiers. Could you please tell us whether you saw, later that day, Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was at dusk or in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us where it was when you had this meeting -- or when you met him, I should say.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this same place as the previous -- as where the previous time he informed me of what I was supposed to do, namely, to stay in front of the building where my office was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was the occasion for Colonel Beara to pay this visit to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He probably knew what inter alia was my duty. So that what he confided in me was because he believed, I think, that I would carry out the job the way he ordered me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. When you met him, did you inform him about your results from the questioning of the various individuals, including Resid Sinanovic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Colonel Beara made any inquiries as to whether you had questioned anyone; and if so, whether you had obtained any relevant or vital information?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me whether anything had happened. No, we said, there was nothing interesting. People had gone to the school, and that was about it as far as our conversation was concerned. We -- it was just one sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Would you repeat your answer again, and please speak slowly so that the interpreters can catch every sentence.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During our next meeting, he asked me: Have you done anything today? And I just told him: Well, they have brought in several people, but it's okay, none of them are discredited people. And that was more or less it. And then they went to the school and the story ended there. There was nothing more to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, after that, did you do anything with Colonel Beara? Did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please describe to us where.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, before we started, we exchanged a couple of sentences to the effect that it was not really secure to bring this number of prisoners into a city where there were no troops. So he told me: Well, it's okay. Let's go for a stroll. So we set off in front of the building where my office was and walked down the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, kindly slow down. Kindly slow down. They have to interpret. We don't want to overburden the people that are translating you, so kindly slow down.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I thought that I was slow enough. So we set off together on foot in front of the building where my office was, in the direction of the elementary school. So we eventually arrived in this street which is nearby the bus station and leads from it directly to the elementary school which is called the Branko Radicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that the same school that was called Vuk Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that it is. When I gave my earlier statements, I wasn't sure which school was which, but in the meantime, before I came here, I inquired, so I found out that indeed it was this school, Branko Radicevic. Probably the name was only changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
