utterances.text: Can you tell us first of all what you observed when you were there, taking this stroll with Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I observed some vehicles, trucks, that is to say cargo trucks and normal trucks -- and buses, sorry, which were full of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what were those people doing?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing specific. They were sitting in these vehicles, either with their buses or other vehicles. The street was full of these vehicles all the way up to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you know who these people were that were in those vehicles, the buses, the trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Clearly they were Muslims, people that had been taken prisoner or people who had surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you know whether there were women and children in those buses as well as men?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see a single woman or a single child.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you saw those buses and trucks full of Muslim males, did you have any particular conversation with Colonel Beara, who, after all, was the head of security of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what you two talked about.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Irrespective of the fact that he was a high-ranking security officer, I felt free to ask him why these vehicles with the people in them had not been transported immediately to where they were supposed to go, which is to say to territory controlled by Muslim troops, why they had these people sitting there waiting in our territory, around the school and so on. It seemed they had already boarded these buses, why hadn't they already been taken to their destination?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was his response?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His response was that that was because a re-organisation of the transport had to be carried out. In other words, there were too many people per vehicle, and that on the return trip those vehicles that had taken women and children to Kladanj, once those vehicles returned, a better organisation or a re-organisation of the transportation of people had to be undertaken and that they would be transported then to Kladanj or elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice who was securing these buses and trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly men, i.e., soldiers, similarly dressed as the people who had brought in the group of people that I referred to earlier. It was already dark, it was dusk, and I cannot be 100 per cent sure that these were people who were not members of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice whether there were any members from the Bratunac Brigade, in particular members of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade? For surely you would have recognised their faces in light of the fact that your office was in the same building where the military police were housed.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have recognised such persons, had there been any, because I knew the military police members and many other soldiers as well. However, perhaps I failed to say something before. I did not go to the very end of the street, but I stopped before the school, in front of the school, and Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Beara, he went on. And I could see that the street leading to the municipality, there was some soldiers in camouflage uniforms similar to the ones that we wore. But it was dusk, so I allowed for the possibility of those people being even members of the military police, but I can't be sure being at this distance of 50 metres or so. But by the vehicles that came there were only and exclusively members of some other units. I'm referring to the vehicles which were parked in the street with the people inside or on those vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you -- when Colonel Beara gave you that explanation, would you please tell us what his demeanor was like. How did he appear?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you believe Colonel Beara when he told you that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we've heard testimony here that Colonel Beara enjoyed, perhaps on occasion, perhaps frequently, the taste for whiskey. Would you happen to know whether on that particular evening when you were with Colonel Beara, whether he was -- whether he had been drinking?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in front of me. He could not have had a drink in the courtyard or on the street. Whether he had had a drink somewhere else, I don't know. However, I believe that I'm experienced enough to recognise a person who had been drinking. I don't know. I don't think so. I can't be sure and I can't talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sorry, he did not -- did he appear sober?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before departing with Colonel Beara, did you by any chance sit and have a drink with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about how long it took for you to walk with Colonel Beara to make your observations. How long were you with him?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We arrived in that street where the vehicles were parked in front of the police building, and it had taken us about 15 metres [as interpreted]. The street is about 500 metres long. I walked behind him. He exchanged a few words with those guards. I was keeping my distance. I didn't want to interfere with his conversations. This is how long it took us, 15 minutes, and then 10 minutes from the police station to the building where we were headed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And about what time would this have been? You said it was getting slightly dark or it was dusk. Do you recall about what time it would have been, in light of the time of year that we're speaking about?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably around 9.00 or half past 9.00, or between half past 8.00 and half past 9.00 p.m. I can't remember exactly. It was already dusk. It was getting dark, and it was that time of the year. And I don't know when it gets dark at that time of year. I know it was already dusk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. After you left Colonel Beara, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And where is your home -- where was your home at that point in time back in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a house; it is an apartment, a bedsitter in an apartment building at the main crossroads in Bratunac. And I've lived there all the time. I still live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, where was it that you left Colonel Beara? What location was it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the sentry at the gate which leads towards the headquarters building. There was a sentry there, in front of that gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would have been back at the Bratunac Brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't enter the courtyard of the building where the headquarters was. I was in front of the gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Celanovic, I'm trying to just get you to tell me: Where was it that you left Colonel Beara, at what location the two of you were. I know that you went home. I just want to know where you parted with Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we returned from the rounds that we had made, I came with him to the gate which is in front of the building where the headquarters was. That's what I said. And only later did I go home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you see Momir Nikolic after that? After meeting with Colonel Beara, did you happen to run into Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you report to anyone what you had seen during this stroll that you had taken with Colonel Beara?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I see -- what I saw the entire town saw and there was no reason for me to inform anybody in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, after going home, did you go out again that night?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Do you know what happened to those people that -- those men that were in those buses and trucks?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please be more precise. Are you referring to that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Celanovic --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's all right. Do you know or have you learned what happened to those men that were in the buses and trucks? Just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us what you know or what you've learned regarding those men that were in those trucks and buses in the school, I would imagine.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were evacuated and transported further on from Bratunac to the territory under the control of Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, you never heard of any of those individuals being executed?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I just asked you what you heard -- what you learned about those men, and now you just told me that they were safely evacuated to the territories. So please tell us what you learned about these men that were in those buses and trucks, if you know.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that they had been transported and that later on many people were killed. It's a well-known fact, unfortunately. These people who had been in Bratunac were subsequently killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us about what time you had learned this; the month, the year.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three, four, or five days later. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know from whom you had learned this information?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Slowly the whole town started talking about that; the troops, the civilians, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in light of your position that you told us about early on, were you ever asked to either participate in an investigation or to question any suspects or witnesses that might have been involved in any of those activities?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked me to participate in any such activity. Nobody was ever brought to me for interrogation about those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you see Colonel Beara after this -- after you learned about what happened to the people?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And so I take it you never had the opportunity to contact him or to speak with him and to ask him what had happened, in light of what he had represented to you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have a single opportunity to talk to him. Maybe even if I had had an opportunity to talk to him, I wouldn't have dared ask him anything. Because I was a foot soldier, a common foot soldier, and it would have been embarrassing for me to ask him about any data or details in addition to the things that he had already told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now I want to switch to another topic. Before I do that, after the 13th, were you ever engaged in questioning anyone else, any other prisoners?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you say you don't remember. I'm talking about the period of the 14th, the 15th, the 16th, the 17th, those days for the rest of July. Do you recall whether you questioned anybody?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that anybody was brought in on any of those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me switch to this other topic, and I want to ask you a couple of questions before I show you a document. After the -- after Dayton, could you please tell us where you were engaged work-wise.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before Dayton, a few days before, at the request of the political structures in Bratunac municipality, I was assigned to perform the tasks and duties of the chief for urban planning, housing, and juridic affairs of Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. As part of your function would you be involved in the occupation of the -- of abandoned property?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was involved in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there any particular legislation at that point in time that controlled the occupation of property that was abandoned?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me show you what has been marked as D170 for identification purposes. If you could please look at it. We have an English translation. First of all, do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a decree of the Government of Republika Srpska regulating the temporary use of houses and office space.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where is it from, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is abandoned property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. This decree itself, where would one locate this particular decree, assuming that it's authentic?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How do we know that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was published in the -- I know because I had the original of the Official Gazette of the Serbian People in which this was published in my hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on this particular document do you see -- is there any notation that this is part of the Official Gazette of the Serbian Peoples in BiH, or BH?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what -- the date of this decree.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Friday, 31 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us whether this decree that was published - and presumably in effect as of 31 July 1992 - whether it was in effect at the time when you were engaged in these activities, that would be sometime after Dayton, which is 1995.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what does this decree do, sir, just very briefly? We don't need a whole legal explanation. Just a comment.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It lists the criteria under which houses and office space may be allocated for temporary use to certain individuals. I'm talking about the temporary use of such buildings, and the individuals have to meet certain criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also, this document prescribes the way of returning such assets to the owners or the state body that owns such property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at Article 9 in particular.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Does Article 9 provide us any guidance as to the ownership or the rights of the rightful owner?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us, what does Article 9, at least in part, tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 9, paragraph 6, reads: "The temporarily allocated housing shall be turned over by the family or person should the owner or tenant return and should there be no space to accommodate the temporary users of such space in view of the size of such accommodation."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me just ask you a hypothetical. If a Muslim family were to abandon its apartment, its rightfully owned apartment, and they wished to, under this decree that was passed on 31 July 1992 that was still in effect after Dayton, under this decree, would that Muslim family be entitled to return to and re-occupy its rightfully owned apartment?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's it for that document. Now, I just have one last document. Very quickly, prior to -- did you know Colonel Blagojevic before he arrived to be -- to take up the post as commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not know each other that well, but I knew that he was Vidoje Blagojevic, brother of my schoolmate, that he was a native of that same place. I knew his mother; I knew who she was. I don't know whether he knew me personally, whether he knew who I was, because we had not lived in the same place for quite a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, before Colonel Blagojevic, did you have -- who was the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel Slavko Ognjenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you get to know him during the period of time when he was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you have a basic opinion as to his character?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Mr. Ognjenovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's who we're talking about, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With apologies to the Trial Chamber, I have to choose my words very carefully when I say that he was not of a good character. And he still is the same; he is a very bad man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: During that period of time, were you ever informed of any policy that he had put in place to basically make the life of the Muslim population in Srebrenica so miserable so that they would leave en masse? Are you aware of any such policies?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you at any point in time participate in a commission organised to review the apartment that he had occupied while he was the commander?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that I was the president of that commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And who ordered the establishment of that commission?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was Commander Blagojevic who ordered that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, what were the reasons for organising that commission?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very simple. That apartment had previously been used by Mr. Ognjenovic, the previous commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The apartment was fully furnished and the furniture belonged to the brigade rather than to the commander. When he was relieved of his duties, Commander Ognjenovic took most of the valuables from the apartment. He didn't actually take them; he attempted to take into his possession most of the valuables. When I say that, I mean he wanted to steal most of the valuable furniture. Why should I spare him? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And -- all right. So on top of being a bad person, he was a thief as well, it would appear, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He tried. He failed. We wouldn't let him succeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you what has been marked as D172 for identification. Just very briefly, do you recognise this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the order for the establishment of a commission which would be tasked with making a list of the furniture in the apartment and their return to the apartment. This commission was tasked with making a record of all that, the apartment was to be sealed, and the key was to be given to the body for security affairs. And there was a deadline by which all this had to be done, and the deadline was the 5th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just one last question: You told us about the character of the previous commander, Ognjenovic. Do you have an opinion as to the character of Colonel Blagojevic when he was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please share that with us.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, as a man, as a human being, he was good and decent and conscientious. As an officer, he was a -- an honourable officer who took, as it were, parental care of all the soldiers, in contrast to the previous commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions and I want to thank you for answering all my questions. Mr. Stojanovic, who represents Mr. Jokic, may have some questions. The Prosecution, I'm sure, will have some, and perhaps even the Judges. If you could answer their questions as truthfully and honestly as you have answered mine, I would most appreciate it. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's time for a break.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Mr. Celanovic. Your Honours, as we have no contiguous points with the account of this particular witness, we have no particular questions for this witness today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any cross-examination? Yes, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I would like to turn to these handwritten notes that you made from your questioning of Resid Sinanovic and the other men. And perhaps if we could turn first to the one that's been marked P476. These are your notes regarding your questioning of Mr. Resid Sinanovic. Now, you've taken a look at this already this morning. I'd like to just draw your attention directly to a few specific areas. Just a few lines down from the top you see where it says: "The army gathered in Kutlici. All imaginable units and able-bodied locals, about 2.000 armed men." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And a little bit further down you see a reference to some commanders who have joined them in Slatina. And there's a reference to "Blagojevic with about 100 policemen." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And a little bit further down, it says: "The column set out for Slatina," and just after that, "Zulfo managed to get out towards Tuzla with a small number of soldiers."

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And then a couple of the references that were brought to your attention earlier this morning: Near the bottom, a reference to "1.000 to 1.500 armed men and about 6.000 to 7.000 others remaining in the spot where the shells landed." Now, my question for you is quite simple: This is not information that is going to help you assess whether Resid Sinanovic is a war criminal or not. In fact, you believe that he wasn't. Is that -- that's correct, right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could turn now to just a couple of your other notes. Prosecution Exhibit 477. You see that in front of you now. Under number 2, the person who was apparently questioned was Munib Dedic. The last point under that, it says something to the effect: "Semso crossed with the group," and then a little later, "with Zulfo to Cerska." Do you recall who Zulfo was in this context?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zulfo is the right name. That is Zulfo Tursunovic, the commander of the army units from Suceska, in Srebrenica, who was listed as a person alleged to have committed war crimes in the village of Podrano and the surrounding villages in 1993, or perhaps the end of 1992, when this village was burnt down and many civilians killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Celanovic. My question for you is, again, quite simple. Now, this information about Semso crossing with the group, or about Zulfo going to Cerska, that has nothing to do with determining whether Munib Dedic is a war criminal or not, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does have something to do with it. Do you want me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Well, you can explain very briefly.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Munib Dedic was first identified as a person who was not a suspect, was not on a known list, at least not the lists which I was using. The next question was: In keeping with Mr. Beara's instruction, for him to tell me if he possibly knew where were the commanders of the units of Naser. Naser is the chief commander. And he told me of one of these names --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: But my question for you is whether this had anything to do with determining whether Munib Dedic was a war criminal. And I think you've already answered that. You said he was not on any lists. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular content has nothing to do with our establishing whether Munib Dedic was a war criminal in itself, but what he told me about the others is linked to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Exactly. And I think what you're saying is that this is in line with Mr. Beara's instructions to know where these other commanders of units of Naser -- where they were. And thank you for that explanation. Now I would like to turn to another one of these notes that you took. And this is Prosecution Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- 478. Yes, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I am addressing the Court for leave to -- if you grant it to me, I should like to rectify something that the Prosecutor has said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. Mr. Beara did not task me with finding about the whereabouts of Naser's units, but the whereabouts -- not even the whereabouts, but if possibly some of these people were brought before me, I asked just in case, because it was not a question of finding out the whereabouts of the units. As regards the whereabouts of the units, this was something I found out from the spontaneous accounts of the people whom I talked to, those who were brought before me. So I just noted down what they said to me, I did not ask them any specific questions to that effect, except perhaps asking whether they maybe knew whether Naser's units were. There was no specific instruction to that effect to me on the part of Mr. Beara. I apologise, perhaps I misunderstood the comment of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, thank you for your explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: But just -- now it's not on the screen anymore, but just a minute ago you said you asked: Where were the commanders of units of Naser. And that is a direct quote. That's what you just said a minute ago. So with your explanation I'm going to continue now to this next document. And in connection with what you've just said, if we look at Prosecution Exhibit 478. And this has to do with notes of Mr. Hasib Ibisevic. And just to note, Mr. Celanovic, you are, of course, permitted to explain, but we hope that you would focus on the specific question that's before us. Now, on this document you see somewhere near the bottom the phrase: "A number of people wished to break through to the Drina to surrender to Serbia." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't. Maybe I'm looking at the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Does your document have the number at the top 0 -- I'm sorry at the bottom, 00678845?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is kindly requested to slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, let me just read it for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And for the interpreters, I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So do you see now where it says: "A number of people wish to break through to the Drina to surrender to Serbia"?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, this, of course, is a piece of information that doesn't name any commanders or name any potential war criminals or anything. It's simply a piece of information about a movement of a number of people, isn't it? It's a simple question, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Can I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Prosecutor, you have extracted one sentence from its context. It says here that a member of the soldier from the -- a member from the army from December 1993 was a member of the unit of Mrki Mandzo and the nicknames of Mandzic. And the Mandzics were on my list, so it was sufficient for me that he mentioned this. So you could not have known this, what the entire context of this whole thing was, but he did mention one of those persons as having been a member of the paramilitary company, a member of his units. So this second sentence cannot be commented without that being brought in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. And thank you for the explanation regarding that second sentence about Mrki Mandzo. My question, of course, was about that last one -- about that last comment, and that is the reference to the number of people going towards the Drina to surrender to Serbia. Now, simply that question about the number of people going to the Drina to surrender to Serbia, that doesn't have anything to do with any specific commander. It doesn't name a commander, does it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is just a spontaneous account of the person who was making -- giving the statement. I never asked him the question: Are there any people who want to cross over to Serbia? He himself of his own accord told me what he knew about the situation in the field, that there was some people wanting to surrender along a stretch of 50 kilometres. And frankly speaking, the people were in fear. And I could see that half of these statements were not true as regards the units, the strength of the units, because people were in fear, so they told me these things in order to avoid coming to any harm. And they couldn't have come to any harm, as far as I was concerned, not from my part. So these were the persons that I had identified and found out to have -- to be clean. These were the circumstances under which this was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- sorry, Mr. Shin. I think really you have to slow down a little bit, because the interpreters and the court reporter are really having a difficult time to follow you. There's no point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. My apologies, Mr. President. I will certainly go more slowly. And my apologies too to the interpreters and the reporter as well about speaking too quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, are you aware that the movement of armed Muslim men and -- armed or unarmed Muslim men from the Srebrenica enclave was the subject of intelligence reports and other reports from the brigade, the Bratunac Brigade, and the Drina Corps level at about the time of the 12th and the 13th of July? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that both civilians and the troops moved through the territory of the Srebrenica enclave. Those who had not surrendered, that is. Now, whether the intelligence organs sent any reports and to whom, I don't know that; nobody had the obligation to inform me about that, as the lowest in rank, and I really had no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So when you were speaking to these people, you didn't have any interest in where the enemy was? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that sense. Of course I wanted to know where the enemy was. But my instructions were to do a different job, and I abided by those instructions, which was just to establish the identity of those persons and whether possibly they were suspicious.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you've told us a couple things about what your instructions were. But maybe just to move on, your explanation -- one of your explanations was that this information about movements of groups of people, armed or unarmed, were spontaneous statements by these people. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So what you're telling us all this information comes from, not because you asked any questions, you who have experience in asking this kind of questioning and gathering this kind of information, not because you asked those questions but because these were spontaneous statements from these people?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Will the Court please draw the attention of the interpreter to the fact that I can't manage to follow. He is speaking -- she is speaking too fast. As far as I managed to understand the question, their statements were a result of the question which I asked them, which was: Do you know where the commanders of Naser's units are? Now, speaking about the -- their knowledge as to -- answering that particular question, whether they knew or not, they would give me a spontaneous account of things, which would then be reflected in my note. And the entire exchange took some 2 to 3 minutes. I hope this time I managed to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. If I could -- and I'll take this slow. If I could just check if I understand that. Did you or did you not ask them where the commanders of Naser's units were?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked them where the commanders of Naser's units were. May I continue? After I identified -- established the identity of the persons that I was addressing, that those were indeed the persons that I was to question, I would ask them what they thought -- only after having established that I asked them what they thought about the situation in the field and whether they knew where Naser's units were. But only after I would establish that they -- the persons in question were clean and were not alleged to have done anything, only after that was established, in fact, I would proceed to ask them whether they knew where these units were. And I would ask them nothing more. And then after they gave me their answer, I would tell them: Okay. You're free to go. I have nothing more to ask you. And this was my attitude toward all of them. And Mr. Sinanovic was a slight exception, because I told you he was already on the list as a person alleged to have done something. But as I also already explained, it was clear that that was not the case, that he was being treated as such on the basis of a couple of statements of some old lady who no longer had her senses about her. I apologise for talking too much and trying to clarify this procedure, my actions, what it was that I asked of these people to tell me, and that is why I am a bit verbose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. So after you established their identity, then you asked them where the units were. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I have to rectify -- correct you again. I didn't ask them where the units were but where the commanders of the unit were. Because they could have -- the units were not the suspicious thing, but the people on the list, the commanders of the units, and the question always referred to them, where were the commanders of Naser's units, and not where the units were. And then they would start to spontaneously respond to my question the way they saw it. I could not be as precise as perhaps as today in this court. It was just an ordinary question, and I just asked them to tell me what they knew without an interruption, without any additional questions. And I know -- I knew, believe me, I knew that those people were in fear of what lays in store for them. And I knew that perhaps half of the things which they were saying were not true, but just were statements made in fear so that I did not set a great store by either the figures or the facts which they gave me to, precisely only to that. Of course they had no reason to fear me. I was very correct in treating them, but they came there already afraid, which was only natural, given the circumstances, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, apart from on this day when you questioned Resid Sinanovic and these other men, apart from these notes that we've looked at, were there other people who were brought before you in front of the Bratunac Brigade to be questioned by you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that anybody else was brought. I remember these people because of Resid and this entire group because of the circumstances which require of me to try and remember everything that had transpired particularly in that connection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, you knew that there were people being held in the Vuk Karadzic school. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: In fact, you knew that there were -- there were hundreds being held there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that there were hundreds.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Well, you told -- you told the police in the Republika Srpska in August of 2003 in your statement that there were hundreds in that school at that time. Do you recall that? We can refer to that, if that would help you.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you recall that, then?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, just for one point of clarification, there's been a -- been reference to a reception centre for these men who were being detained and also a school. And we know about the Vuk Karadzic school. We're talking now about the building, all those terms are used to identify the building in July 1995 that was known as the Vuk Karadzic school. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The reception centre, the school, it's all the same. To my mind the school was the reception centre for the people who had surrendered, who were brought in. There was no other facility, or at least I was not aware of any such facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, are you aware that in May of 1992 that school was also used as a place for detention of Muslims from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And were you aware that a number of people, a number of Muslims, were killed at that time at that school?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you think -- did it occur to you when these men came to be questioned by you and when they knew they were going to that school, do you think that might have caused them any fear or concern, knowing the history of that place in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they felt, whether they were afraid or not. But I knew that while they were by me they did not have anything to fear because I treated them correctly. I don't know whether they were afraid of anything that might happen after they left me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, these hundreds of men in the Vuk Karadzic school, did you go and question any of them to determine whether any of them were war criminals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This would not have made any sense. It would have been pointless. May I explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instruction or the order to me was to interrogate just those people that were brought to the police building, if they were indeed brought in. This group consisting of six or seven people, whose notes I have in front of me, was brought not for me to interrogate them, but this group of soldiers stopped by the building to ask where the school was. Then I introduced myself and I explained what my role was to these soldiers. And then when I realised what was going on, it would have been pointless for me to try and establish the identity of the people who were brought to me by pure chance. And at the same time hundreds and thousands of people were brought to a different place and nobody interrogated them. This would have been a very random way of doing things, so I did not go and interrogate anybody because it would have been pointless. Such a procedure on my part would have been absurd and unnecessary. It never occurred to me to engage in an activity like that. Hundreds and thousands of people passed through with any -- without any control. Why would I choose just a few to establish their identity and interrogate them whilst all the others passed through unidentified?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Celanovic, you've mentioned now hundreds and thousands of people being brought to other -- to a different place or different places and being detained. Did it occur to you that perhaps you could have gotten a list of these people, their names?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned hundreds or maybe thousands. This is my assumption. Later on I learned that several thousands of Muslims were killed. I said hundreds or thousands. But what happened in Bratunac, in the school, I could see people on the windows from the street. I could see empty vehicles in front of the school from which people were taken to the school. And as just a normal individual, I could make an assessment as to how many people could fit in the school, how many vehicles were in the streets. So I could tell, based on that, that there were several hundreds at the moment when I was observing the situation. When I said "hundreds or thousands," I only learned later on -- everybody knows today how many went missing. That's why I said hundreds or thousands. Secondly, how can a person in the course of such a day identify so many people and make a sensible list out of that? It would have been physically impossible. And I did not have any such instruction as to maybe leave my office or the premises and go and interview all these Muslims in order to make some sort of a list. I hope I've made myself clear with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Celanovic, were you aware of any list of people being detained anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, can you please slow down. Can you please repeat the question. I didn't understand the question, and please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I will speak very slowly. The question was actually quite brief. Do you know whether there was any list of any of these Muslim detainees at that time? Around the 13th of July, did such a list exist, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have no knowledge of any such list or lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, apart from your questioning of Mr. Resid Sinanovic, your friend, and these other men, were you aware of any other interviews being conducted to determine whether any of these detainees were war criminals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you -- my next question you may have indirectly answered previously, but just so we're clear: At some point you decided that it wasn't worthwhile for you to try to determine whether any particular Muslim detainee was a war criminal or not. Right?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And I think you have explained - please correct me if I'm wrong - one of the reasons was because you knew -- or to the best of your knowledge, nobody was checking -- nobody was doing anything similar, nobody was checking any of these detainees to see if they were war criminals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I knew that nobody was checking. I didn't know if anybody was checking. I didn't know that. I didn't know for a fact that nobody was checking. I said I didn't know if it was checked. Now, the decision that I made, at one point after these people left for the school, I made a break, I went to my apartment to change my clothes because it was very hot. On my way back in that street I was close to the baker's, and I saw what I saw. And after that I decided it was pointless, even if somebody was brought to me to continue interrogating them, because I realised that there were too many people for all of them to be identified. I was not aware of anybody who would have had a similar order or instruction. And that's when I decided that this was beside the point, that it didn't make any sense for me to continue doing that, even if people were brought in. And luckily enough, nobody was brought to me on that day in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So, as you just explained to us, there were too many people even to identify them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection. It's been -- first of all, it's been asked and answered. And now he's trying to fit the, you know, the square peg into the round hole so he can make his closing argument. He's not being fair with the gentleman. But in any event, I stick to my previous remark: It's been asked and it's been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shin, I think you've made your point already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Shall we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Very well. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you tell Mr. Beara that you thought it didn't make any sense, that it was absurd to try to interview people as he had told you to regarding the identity of war criminals?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He never asked me anything about that. He just asked me a general question: Did you do anything today? I told him: Yes, there were a few people. And then he said: Okay, kiddo, let's move on. That's the way he used to address me. He didn't expect any such information from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move on to -- I'm sorry. Thank you for that answer. I'd like to just move on to the next point now. When these people were brought to you, both -- I'm sorry, these five or six people that you questioned, when they were brought to you in front of your office, one of the soldiers who brought them, maybe one or more of them, asked the military police where the school was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They asked everybody. There were a few soldiers who did not belong to the military police, one or two of them, and there were maybe three military policemen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And these few soldiers they asked who were not part of the military police, they were with the Bratunac Brigade, were they not?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe we misunderstood each other, but you're talking about the people who are asking where the school was, correct, when you say that they're obviously not from the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So my question is just this: Someone from the military police then explained to them where the school was. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody explained to them where the school was. I can't remember who it was who said to those soldiers that the school was down the road. Somebody did say that, I don't remember who that was, but there's something I told them. And if you want me to, I can tell you what I told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If you could briefly, please go ahead, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly. I said to these lads what my task was, what my role was. They just happened to be there, and I told them that I should ask for these people's IDs, and they agreed to that. I told them that in my office at that time there was another person, Resid Sinanovic namely, and I asked them that after my conversation with these people that they had brought in, that they should leave some time for my colleague who was in the office and to escort him to the school as well. And they said okay, and that's exactly what happened later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: My question was just about who had given them the directions. Now, do you remember telling the Republika Srpska police in your August of 2003 interview that it was one of the military police who explained where the school was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was somebody from the military police, but I don't know his name. I was under the impression that you wanted me to tell you the name, and I don't remember the name. There were two or three military policemen, and there was no reason for me to remember any of their names. We were talking at cross-purposes. I thought you were asking me about the name of the person who told them where the school was. Well, the -- all three of them were talking at the same time. They were pointing towards the school with their hands, and it was very difficult for me to be sure of who it was that provided these soldiers with the information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Since we perhaps misunderstood each other, let me be very clear: It was someone from the military police -- the Bratunac Brigade military police - not the name, but someone from the military police - who told these men where the school was. Is that correct? Not the name now --

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not absolutely sure. Somebody said that, and I believe that he was a member of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade. Despite all my wishes, I cannot be sure of that, and I can't tell you with certainty something that I'm not sure of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, did you see -- as they left, did you see that these men brought these five or six detainees to the school, or was that something you couldn't see from where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see that the vehicle carrying these people went towards the main road, the Gavrilo Princip road, as it is known today, and that it started driving to the right looking from where I was observing. I was standing on the stairway with my back turned towards the military police building. This right-hand side road leads towards the bus station and on towards the elementary school. My further view was obstructed by the houses, by the trees.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: These soldiers came back to where your office was, or right in front of your office, about five or ten minutes later but without their detainees. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And not all the soldiers came back. Two or three returned, and one of them told me that they are here to assist the military police. And I didn't comment upon that. They just told me that they were here to provide assistance to the military police, if that would be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall if they said something else about what the nature of that assistance would be or was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall telling the police of the Republika Srpska in August of 2003 what that -- what the nature of that assistance was?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been my assumption. Since they had this vehicle, I assumed that they would provide assistance with the transportation. I don't know what other assistance could they have provided. They had a vehicle, and that's what -- the way I understood their sentence or two sentences that they said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, when you gave the statement to the RS police in August of 2003, they cautioned you to tell the truth, correct, the police?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: They cautioned you not to leave out any information, correct? And as a lawyer you may be familiar with these cautions in your system.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: They cautioned you that there could be a criminal penalty for any false testimony, correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: They told you that this was in connection with an investigation into Srebrenica in 1995, and that's a serious investigation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... circumstances as a lawyer, or perhaps as anyone, you would want to be as accurate and complete as possible, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As accurate as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So I'm going to read to you -- and if you would like to see it, just please let me know, I'm happy to put that in front of you as well -- what -- I'm sorry. Just one minute, please, with your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the gentleman could be provided with a copy of his statement, I think that would be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm happy to do that. This is a document marked Prosecution Exhibit 859/A for the English version and B for the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, please bear in mind that you are being interpreted into two languages and the interpreters do not have a copy of what you are reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters not for getting this to them earlier. It is a very brief sentence and I will read very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, I would like to direct you to the very last page of that statement. First of all, do you recognise this as the record of the statement that you gave in August 2003?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you see your name and signature at the bottom. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, the sentence I would like to direct you to --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Sorry, just one minute, with your indulgence, Your Honours. I'm sorry, it's -- I had the wrong page there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If you could turn to what is page -- the second page in which your statement is written, and that constitutes the fourth page from the very beginning. Now, two-thirds of the way down this page and just above that paragraph break where there is a blank space, and in the Serbian version you'll see that the sentence I'm referring to begins [B/C/S spoken]. And I'll read in the English: "The soldiers took the group and put them in the school. In about five or ten minutes" -- sorry. I'll go slowly. "In about five or ten minutes they came back to the military police building and said that they had been ordered to assist the military police of the Bratunac Brigade for similar cases since they now knew where the reception centre was and they had a vehicle for that purpose." Do you see that sentence -- I'm sorry, those two sentences?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So when you gave that statement, trying to be as accurate and complete as possible, that's what you told the RS police what these soldiers with the truck had told you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Celanovic, just moving on a little, you had said earlier that I believe - and please correct me if I'm wrong - that you did not recognise anyone from the Bratunac Brigade in front of the Vuk Karadzic school. Is that right, or have I gotten that wrong?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recognise anybody from the Bratunac Brigade in front of the Vuk Karadzic school. Nobody whose name I would know, but judging by the uniforms that I saw at a distance of 50 to 60 metres, I believed that they belonged to the Bratunac Brigade. I recognised the cheap, thin, camouflage uniforms, unlike the uniforms that I saw on the lads that were standing guard in front of the school itself. It was different. It was of the kind that only American troops have. It was dusk, and it was very difficult for me to say that I saw certain individuals whom I knew, but I believed that they were members of the Bratunac Brigade, judging by nothing else but their uniforms that I saw at a distance. That is what I saw in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And so you believe -- just to be clear, you believe that the persons that you saw in front of the school were members of the Bratunac Brigade. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the persons, not in front of the school but in this short street and at the end of the street which leads towards the school. So it's a little bit further on, next to the municipality building which housed the archives. I don't know whether you have referred to this particular building at all so far, but I'm trying to be precise in explaining this. So to the right-hand side observed in the direction of the school, this is where I could see them. I wasn't paying too much attention really. Had I known that I would be taking the stand here today, I would have made it my business to indeed remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you referred to that short street where you saw some members of the Bratunac Brigade, that's the street along which the buses and trucks were parked. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, just to make it simple, have you heard -- maybe you didn't see at that time, but did you hear later that there were Bratunac Brigade military police guarding the Vuk Karadzic school on that day -- on that evening?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that some of them performed that duty as well. As to how many there were, when this was, I don't know this. I only heard later that some of them had secured the building. I don't know which of these lads they were. This is something that I heard only later in informal exchanges.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Do you recall who told you that, even informally?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. These were just leisurely talks which were a long time after these events had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Did you hear anything, either that evening or the next morning, about bodies, 50 bodies, of Muslims being found at that Vuk Karadzic school or in one of the buildings right behind it?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything about that. I hear it for the first time, that bodies were found either in the school or around the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So you never heard that there were people killed at that school either on the 12th or the 13th or the 14th?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, are you aware -- are you aware that there were Bratunac Brigade -- I'm sorry. Let me rephrase that. Mr. Celanovic, you were aware that the Bratunac Brigade military police escorted these buses and trucks to Zvornik, these buses and trucks that were full of men in the streets of Bratunac that night. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that they escorted them from my conversations with military policemen, but I didn't see. So I heard from them that they had been also among those who were escorted -- among those who escorted the convoy were also members of the Bratunac military police brigade. And I believe ...

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And when you say your conversations with military policemen, you mean military policemen from the Bratunac Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in what context this particular question was asked. Can I have a more precise formulation of the question? What particular conversation are we referring to? The informal conversation that I referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Actually, I mean the conversation that you just talked about, the conversation with military policemen who told you that there were Bratunac Brigade military policemen who escorted these buses and trucks to Zvornik. Now, you had that conversation with military policemen, you said, and I just wanted to clarify that those are Bratunac Brigade military policemen. You nodded. If you could please say yes or no into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is all right. Yes, these were military police of the -- military police of the -- Bratunac Brigade military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn back briefly to a conversation that you described that you had with Colonel Beara, as you say, in which he explained to you why there were buses and trucks in Bratunac that evening. You told us just a few minutes ago that when you were trying to assess how many people there were in the Vuk Karadzic school, you saw the empty vehicles in front of the Vuk Karadzic school, the vehicles which you believed these men were -- had been brought on. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several vehicles that I saw, but there were also others that I didn't see. We are not talking about the same street here, are we? Could you please be more precise. I don't mind drawing you a sketch to show you what street we are talking about. There was a street full of buses and other vehicles with people on them. And there is a small street leading towards the municipality on the right. There is one to the left, towards the stadium and towards Suha settlement. There are two streets. There were a few empty vehicles in the street on the left which leads by the stadium. And I saw two or three vehicles that could be seen from where I was standing. Since the street is sloping, there may have been more. And before that, I saw a longer street full of vehicles. And from the market, I also could see that around the stadium and in the stadium there were vehicles full of people; that's what I'm talking about. I'm trying to be as precise as possible here, as much as I can, as much as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And we do understand that, Mr. Celanovic. If I could make the question very simple, and I think you have explained that in your answer just now; you did see some empty vehicles in the street. And let's set aside the question now of where exactly they were.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was that a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just explained where they were. In that street on the left, at the crossroads. Why don't you give me a piece of paper. I'd like to draw it to you. I can't explain. As I'm facing the school, there is a street which leads to the gate of the school. And on the left from that place there is a street which leads by the stadium, and on the right there is a short street leading towards the municipality building. In the street on the left I saw two, three, four -- I can't be more precise than that, I didn't count the vehicles. That's how many vehicles I saw. But since the street is sloping, I can assume that there were more streets [as interpreted] towards the bottom of the road. I was standing there for a minute and then I returned. But there is another fact, and the fact is that I saw many more vehicles in a different place and that I could see people on the windows of the school. That is another fact. And that's where I saw a lot of vehicles that I couldn't count. But having seen all of these vehicles and knowing how many classrooms there are, if you can do your maths you can calculate how many people fit in the school. I know exactly how big the schoolrooms are, and any layman by doing their maths could tell you how many people there were in the school. At the moment when I was observing the situation, I believe there were several hundreds of people in the school plus the people in the vehicles that I've just mentioned. I really don't see how I can explain it in any different way. I can't give you the precise number either. The fact is that I've given you the essence of what I saw. I really don't know what other details or precisions you want from me. If you can be more precise in your questions, I will answer. Your questions start to tire me, really. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, I think the question put to you is very simple. That is: Did you see some empty vehicles in the street? It's a very, very simple question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I explained in very simple words that I saw three or four empty vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Celanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, do you recall your conversation with Mr. Beara where he told you why it was that these buses and trucks with men on them could not leave, or why they were staying in Bratunac? Do you remember that? Just, please, yes or no on that question.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And he explained to you that they were waiting because there was a re-organisation of transportation because there were too many people on some or more than some of the buses and trucks. Do you remember that? Just, please, yes or no unless I've made something significantly wrong here.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, did that explanation make sense to you, in light of the empty buses that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Celanovic, there's no reason why some of those buses couldn't have gone to Kladanj, is there? Some or maybe all of them?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN CELANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no reason why they should not have gone to Kladanj. They could have gone to Kladanj if such a decision had been made.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not sure, but this may be a good place to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could I ask, how long are you going to do your cross-examination for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I would hope for no more than 20 minutes or so, I would hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid that we have to break now, and we'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
